transcript.content:
A user has filed a support ticket reporting that their experience
with the service has degraded — requests feel slow or are failing
for them. The on-call team needs you to investigate.

Telemetry parquets are stored in: `.`
Available files: abnormal_metrics.parquet, abnormal_traces.parquet,
abnormal_logs.parquet, abnormal_metrics_histogram.parquet,
abnormal_metrics_sum.parquet, normal_metrics.parquet,
normal_traces.parquet, normal_logs.parquet.

Walk the telemetry to identify which endpoints / services are
actually affected, then determine the root cause(s) of the
degradation.

input.query: SELECT 'abn' src, service_name, span_name, count(*) n, avg(duration)/1e6 avg_ms, quantile_cont(duration,0.95)/1e6 p95_ms, sum(CASE WHEN attr_status_code='Error' OR attr_http_response_status_code>=500 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) errs FROM abnormal_traces GROUP BY 1,2,3 UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', service_name, span_name, count(*), avg(duration)/1e6, quantile_cont(duration,0.95)/1e6, sum(CASE WHEN attr_status_code='Error' OR attr_http_response_status_code>=500 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) FROM normal_traces GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY 2,3,1

input.reflection: Abnormal vs normal: loadgenerator/ui-dashboard latency up ~5-7x on travel plan / travel / preserve endpoints. Downstream services with big jumps: ts-seat-service (avg 19ms -> 840ms, p95 22 -> 3465ms, 0 HTTP errors), ts-travel-service (36 -> 980ms), ts-route-plan (165 -> 2764), ts-travel-plan (191 -> 3288), ts-preserve (170 -> 1002). Services like auth, config, order, price, user are unchanged. Hypothesis: seat-service (leaf-ish, called by travel/preserve) is the origin; need to confirm via parent/child span relationships and pod-level metrics (CPU/GC/threads) for seat-service vs travel-service.

input.reflection: Span-tree evidence: travel-service -> seat-service left_tickets takes ~2125ms; inside seat-service, SeatController.getLeftTicketOfInterval takes ~1136ms of which the only identified child (config-service GET configs) takes ~6ms. So ~1100ms is spent in seat-service's own code/dependencies not visible as child spans (e.g., DB, lock, GC, thread pool). Seat-service JVM metrics: jvm.cpu.time lower in abnormal (9.4 vs 27 avg), container.cpu.time slightly higher; heap similar. Not obviously GC/heap. Next: seat-service logs (errors/warnings), and seat-service pod-level metrics (abnormal_metrics: cpu throttling, memory, connection pools).

SELECT date_trunc('minute', time) minute, count(*) n, sum(CASE WHEN duration>1000000000 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) over1s, round(quantile_cont(duration,0.5)/1e6,1) p50, round(quantile_cont(duration,0.95)/1e6,1) p95, round(max(duration)/1e6,1) max_ms FROM abnormal_traces WHERE service_name='ts-seat-service' AND span_name='POST /api/v1/seatservice/seats/left_tickets' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

SELECT date_trunc('minute', time) AS mn, count(*) AS n, sum(CASE WHEN duration>1000000000 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS over1s, round(quantile_cont(duration,0.5)/1e6,1) AS p50, round(quantile_cont(duration,0.95)/1e6,1) AS p95, round(max(duration)/1e6,1) AS max_ms FROM abnormal_traces WHERE service_name='ts-seat-service' AND span_name='POST /api/v1/seatservice/seats/left_tickets' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

SELECT 'abn' src, p.span_name client_span, c.service_name child_svc, count(*) n, round(avg(p.duration)/1e6,1) client_ms, round(quantile_cont(p.duration,0.5)/1e6,1) client_p50, round(avg(c.duration)/1e6,1) server_ms, round(quantile_cont(c.duration,0.5)/1e6,1) server_p50 FROM abnormal_traces p JOIN abnormal_traces c ON c.parent_span_id=p.span_id AND c.trace_id=p.trace_id WHERE p.service_name='ts-seat-service' AND p.span_name='POST' GROUP BY 1,2,3 UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', p.span_name, c.service_name, count(*), round(avg(p.duration)/1e6,1), round(quantile_cont(p.duration,0.5)/1e6,1), round(avg(c.duration)/1e6,1), round(quantile_cont(c.duration,0.5)/1e6,1) FROM normal_traces p JOIN normal_traces c ON c.parent_span_id=p.span_id AND c.trace_id=p.trace_id WHERE p.service_name='ts-seat-service' AND p.span_name='POST' GROUP BY 1,2,3

SELECT 'abn' src, metric, service_name, count(*) n, round(avg(sum/nullif(count,0)),3) avg_per_call, round(max(max),3) mx, round(sum(sum)/nullif(sum(count),0),3) mean FROM abnormal_metrics_histogram GROUP BY 1,2,3 UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', metric, service_name, count(*), round(avg(sum/nullif(count,0)),3), round(max(max),3), round(sum(sum)/nullif(sum(count),0),3) FROM normal_metrics_histogram GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY 2,3,1

input.reflection: Key new evidence: (1) ts-seat-service is a single pod (ts-seat-service-675c89f44-95mwp). Its p50 is unchanged (~11ms) but the tail is huge (p95 ~3-6s, max 64s) for left_tickets. (2) Seat's outbound client spans ('POST') to ts-order-service take avg 1859ms (p50 5ms) while the order-service server span is only 3ms — so ~1.8s of latency is spent in seat-service before/around the outbound HTTP call, not in order-service. Seat CPU is LOW (0.14 vs 0.49 normal) and queueSize lower, so not CPU saturation — suggests thread/connection-pool blocking or a stall inside seat. (3) ts-travel-service db.client.connections.use_time mean 1602ms (normal 96ms), max 67s — connection held much longer; travel calls seat (2125ms) and has its own DB. Need: travel-service children breakdown (DB vs seat), and whether travel's slowness is entirely attributable to seat. Also check order-service pod CPU/memory to rule it out.

content.text:
## Findings

**Bottom line:** One root cause, with high confidence. The degradation starts on the outbound call from **ts-seat-service to ts-order-service**. Seat's `left_tickets` path stalls for seconds on that call, and every caller up to the user inherits the delay. I did not find evidence of a second independent fault.

### Affected endpoints (user-visible)

Latencies are abnormal-window averages from the loadgenerator spans, compared with the normal window.

| Endpoint (via ts-ui-dashboard) | Abnormal | Normal |
|---|---|---|
| POST /travelplanservice/travelPlan/quickest | ~7.0 s | ~70 ms |
| POST /travelservice/trips/left | ~5.7 s | ~70 ms |
| POST /travelplanservice/travelPlan/minStation | ~5.4 s | ~70 ms |
| POST /travelplanservice/travelPlan/cheapest | ~5.0 s | ~70 ms |
| POST /preserveservice/preserve | ~3.6 s | ~70 ms |

- Errors are rare: about 10 error-status loadgenerator spans in total, so this is mainly a latency SLO violation rather than a hard failure.
- Unaffected: login, user lookups, travel2 trips (~118 ms), food, and most internal services such as auth, config, order, price, user, and route.

### Propagation chain

1. **Origin: ts-seat-service** (single pod `ts-seat-service-675c89f44-95mwp`, node worker6), endpoint `POST /api/v1/seatservice/seats/left_tickets`.
   - The median is unchanged (~11 ms), but the tail is severe: p95 is 3–6 s and max is 64 s.
   - Its handler `SeatController.getLeftTicketOfInterval` averages 1.1 s, versus 29 ms normally.
2. **Callers inherit the delay:**
   - ts-travel-service → seat: 2.1 s per call (normal ~30 ms)
   - ts-travel-plan-service → seat: 866 ms
   - ts-preserve-service → seat: 510 ms
   - The gap is essentially zero on these edges (for example, 2128 ms client vs 2125 ms server), so the time is spent inside seat.
3. Upstream amplification continues: travel-service and preserve-service slow down, then route-plan-service (quickestRoute ~9.7 s, minStopStations ~8.5 s), then travel-plan-service (~16 s on quickest), then ts-ui-dashboard, then the loadgenerator.

### Pinpointing the fault inside seat

- **The seat → order-service edge is the only broken edge.**
  - Seat's client spans to ts-order-service average **1859 ms**, while the order-service server spans take only **3.2 ms**. Normally the client span is ~8 ms.
  - The ~1.85 s is spent in seat before the request reaches order-service.
- Seat's other outbound calls are fast: the config-service GET is ~7 ms and the order-other-service POST is ~7 ms.
- The order-service pod is healthy: CPU is lower than normal, its spans are 3–5 ms, and it has no error logs.
- Seat is not CPU-saturated (CPU usage ~0.14 vs ~0.49 normal), its GC and thread count are normal, and its node is not saturated.
- Taken together, this points to a stall in seat's outbound path to order-service: a blocked or exhausted HTTP client connection pool, or network latency or loss on the seat → order link. It is not a compute or GC problem.
- Seat logs are INFO only, with no errors. Its HTTP client duration histogram rose from ~3.6 to ~38 ms on average, with a max of ~64 s.

### Secondary observations (not separate root causes)

- ts-travel-service DB connection hold time is elevated (mean 1.6 s vs 96 ms normal). This is consistent with connections being held open across the blocked seat call, not with a database fault. Pending requests stay at 0 and usage stays within the pool of 10.
- Log WARN volume in order-service and order-other-service is similar to normal and is not causal.

### Verification still open

- I could not directly observe the network layer or the seat HTTP client pool metrics. The evidence localizes the fault to seat's outbound path to order-service, but it cannot by itself distinguish a pool-exhaustion cause from a network-latency cause on that link.
